Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a massive right-sided pneumothorax with significant mediastinal shift to the right and an abnormal, bulging cardiac silhouette on the right side. This appearance is characteristic of cardiac herniation into the right pleural cavity (typically following intrapericardial pneumonectomy), where the heart protrudes through a pericardial defect, causing acute hemodynamic compromise due to torsion and obstruction of venous return.
